n: Dual-Use Goods Procurement via Front Companies
ds: Proliferation networks seek controlled or dual-use items through front companies, brokers and intermediaries that disguise the true end user. Financial institutions mainly see this through payments and trade documents, so detection depends on matching customer profile, goods and destination.

src.t: FATF, Guidance on Counter Proliferation Financing (2018)
FATF, Guidance on Proliferation Financing Risk Assessment and Mitigation (2021)

rat: Front companies paying for controlled goods; trade and payment review.

ind.n: Customer or counterparty business inconsistent with technical goods traded
ind.cx: Trading or logistics firm with no technical background transacts in items with possible weapons or missile applications.
ind.fp: Distributors do handle technical goods outside their main specialty.
ind.ds: Trading or logistics firm with no technical background transacts in items with possible weapons or missile applications.

ind.n: End user vague, missing or reluctant to provide details
ind.cx: Customer or counterparty is evasive about final destination, use or end-user certificate.
ind.fp: Commercial confidentiality can explain limited detail.
ind.ds: Customer or buyer is evasive about end use, final destination or end-user certificate, or declines re-export undertakings.
ind.cn: End-user information vague, missing or refused

ind.n: Delivery to freight forwarder, free-trade zone or address unrelated to the buyer
ind.cx: Goods shipped to a forwarder, bonded zone or residential address rather than the end user.
ind.ds: Goods or cards are shipped to freight forwarders, reshippers, mail drops or addresses with no storage or sales operations or link to the buyer.
ind.cn: Delivery to forwarder, mailbox or address unrelated to buyer

ind.cx: Recently formed company with minimal premises or staff, shared address or officers with other trading firms, and large-value technical trades.
ind.fp: Start-ups and virtual offices are legitimate.
ind.ds: Entity has no staff, premises, website or trading history consistent with its stated activity, yet receives significant payments.
ind.cn: Shell entity with no operating footprint

ind.n: Payments from third parties unrelated to the trade
ind.cx: Invoices are settled by firms that are not named in trade documents, often from high-risk or diversion-prone jurisdictions.
ind.fp: Treasury centres and group payment arrangements are common.
ind.ds: Payments are made by parties with no apparent link to the underlying transaction, goods or services.
ind.cn: Payments from or for third parties unrelated to the underlying trade

ind.n: Price or specification not in line with commercial norms
ind.cx: Equipment priced far above or below market, or specifications altered to fall below control thresholds.
ind.fp: Prices vary with customisation and volume.
ind.ds: Equipment priced far above or below market, or specifications altered to fall below control thresholds.

ind.n: Orders for items matching procurement watch lists or inquiries
ind.cx: Goods, parties or addresses match published alerts by export-control or enforcement authorities.
ind.fp: List data may be dated or generic.
ind.ds: Goods, parties or addresses match published alerts by export-control or enforcement authorities.

ind.n: Use of multiple intermediaries or repeated changes of consignee
ind.cx: Shipments are re-routed or re-invoiced through successive parties.
ind.ds: Shipments or cargoes are re-routed, re-invoiced or have ownership shifted through successive parties without clear commercial reason.
ind.cn: Repeated change of consignee or buyer in transit

ctl.ds: Screens goods descriptions, HS codes and items against export-control, precursor and procurement watch lists, with access to technical review. It catches proliferation-sensitive and restricted goods.

ctl.n: Counterparty capacity and trade profile assessment
ctl.ds: Tests whether a counterparty's size, history, equipment and sector make the traded volume and goods plausible, and models an expected trade profile to alert on deviation. It detects trading that is out of line with the business.

ctl.n: Purpose and intended nature of relationship
ctl.ds: Captures and challenges the stated purpose of the account, expected activity, volumes and geographies at onboarding, creating a baseline against which later behaviour is judged. Vague or implausible answers prompt further enquiry or decline.

ctl.n: Account restriction, decline and exit policy
ctl.ds: Defines when a relationship or supplier must be declined, restricted or terminated, for example for unresolved due diligence, non-cooperation or unmanageable risk, with timelines and approvers. It prevents indefinite continuation of relationships that cannot be controlled.

Requires end-user statements, authenticates their signatories, verifies licences and sites, and obtains post-delivery reports for goods and funds. It confirms that goods or funds reach the stated end use.

Compares shipping routes, ports and delivery points with typical lanes and risk lists, and requests explanation for unusual hubs or indirect delivery. It reveals diversion, transshipment and evasion routing.

Applies targeted enhanced checks to customer types or sectors known to be vulnerable to misuse, such as cash-intensive trades, money service businesses, high-value dealers, professional services, charities or waste handlers. Questions and evidence are tailored to how the sector normally operates.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.

Compares declared unit prices, award values, fees and ancillary costs with reference databases, estimates and comparable contracts, and requires documented rationale for outliers. It detects over- and under-invoicing and inflated awards.

ctl.n: Suspicion escalation and reporting decision protocol
ctl.ds: Defines timelines, owners and criteria for escalating concerns and deciding whether to report, and for documents implying payments to proscribed groups. It ensures timely, accountable decisions.

Alerts on repeated or late amendments to consignee, destination, price or parties in a trade, and re-runs due diligence on changed parties. It detects manipulation of documents to evade controls after approval.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.
